transcript.content: Hello. What brings you into the clinic today?

Hi. Um, well, I’m here because my sleep has basically just fallen apart. I’ll lie in bed in my apartment for hours at night... my laptop will be closed, but I'm still just mentally rechecking everything. You know, work deadlines, tuition payments, class assignments. It just loops. And even when I finally do manage to get to sleep, I wake up feeling like my brain never really turned off.
Do you find yourself struggling with these constant worries during the day as well, or does it mainly happen when you try to sleep?

Yeah, it’s definitely during the day, too. It’s pretty much all the time, honestly. My mind just keeps jumping from one thing to the next. 

Like, I’ll be at my desk and start worrying that I’m falling behind at work, and then that immediately turns into stressing over whether I’m wasting money on school... or, I don't know, worrying that my family will think I just can’t handle things. It feels like every time a small issue comes up, I treat it like it could completely derail my whole future. So, yeah, it doesn't really stop during the day.
About how long have you been dealing with this constant worry?

It's been about... a year and three months, I'd say. It really started right around the time I enrolled in an evening graduate certificate program. I work full-time as a management analyst, so trying to juggle that job during the day and the classes at night... yeah, that's when this all really began.
Aside from feeling constantly worried or stressed, have you been feeling persistently down, sad, or depressed?

No, I wouldn't say I feel sad or depressed. It's really just the stress and the worrying. I mean, I get frustrated that I can't relax, but I don't feel down or anything like that. It's just... my brain is always on high alert, not sad.
Do you find it difficult to control or stop these worries once they start?

Yeah, it's really hard to stop them. I'll... I try to tell myself to just stop and focus on one thing, but it doesn't work. One worry just immediately leads right into another one. Before I know it, I'm checking my calendar, going over my budget, and looking at my assignments over and over again... instead of actually getting any of my work done. I just can't seem to shut it off once it gets going.
Along with all this worry, have you noticed physical symptoms like muscle tension, tightness, or soreness in your body?
No, I haven't really noticed anything like that. Um... I don't feel sore or tight, really. It's mostly just my mind racing all the time, but physically, no, I don't think I have any muscle tension.
Do you often feel restless or keyed up, like you are constantly on edge?

No, I don't think so. I don't feel restless or like I can't sit still. I mean, I sit at my desk all day for work without a problem. It's really just my mind that feels like it's constantly going, not my body. So, no, I wouldn't say I feel keyed up or physically on edge.
Do you find that you have trouble concentrating, or that your mind sometimes goes blank?

Yes, definitely. I have a lot of trouble concentrating. I'll... I'll sit and stare at the same financial model for work, or a class reading, for ages. Then I'll realize I've reread the exact same paragraph like five times without actually absorbing any of it. It's just because my head is already off running through everything that could go wrong instead of what's right in front of me. So, yeah, focusing on one thing is really hard right now.
Do you find yourself becoming easily fatigued or wearing out quickly during the day?

Yes, I do. By mid-afternoon at the office, I just feel completely drained. It gets to the point where even doing something simple, like answering emails or just walking to the subway, takes so much effort. And it's not like I can just sleep it off, either. Even if I rest all weekend, it doesn't seem to give me my energy back. I just feel worn out all the time.
